props.gloss_en: the mishna: [one may tie] the straps of a shoe and a sandal [on Shabbat]
one baraita: one who untied the straps of a shoe or sandal is liable to a sin-offering
another baraita: he is exempt but it is forbidden
another baraita: it is permitted ab initio
the baraita that says liable [for a shoe] speaks of a shoemakers' [knot]
exempt but forbidden [for a shoe] -- of the Rabbis' [shoes]
permitted ab initio [for a shoe] -- of the people of Mechoza
the baraita that says liable [for a sandal] speaks of Arabs' [sandals], which shoemakers tie
exempt but forbidden [for a sandal] -- of the [strap] knots they tie themselves
permitted ab initio [for a sandal] -- a sandal two people go out in
Abaye, asked about a pair of sandals that Rav Yehuda and his child both wore: [untying them renders one] liable to a sin-offering
Rav Yehuda: even 'exempt but forbidden' would be difficult for me, and you say 'liable'?! -- because on weekdays too sometimes I go out in it and sometimes the child does
Abaye: if so, it is permitted ab initio
R' Abbahu to R' Yirmeya, whose sandal strap tore in a karmelit: take a moist reed fit for animal food and wrap it on it
Rav Yosef to Abaye, whose strap tore: leave it
there [R' Yirmeya's sandal in the karmelit] it is not guarded; here it is guarded
Abaye: but it is a vessel, for if I wish I can switch it from right to left
Rav Yosef: conclude from it that the halakha follows R' Yehuda
a sandal whose two ears or two straps broke, or whose whole sole was removed, is pure
one of its ears, or one of its straps, or most of its sole removed -- impure
R' Yehuda: if the inner [strap] broke -- impure
R' Yehuda: the outer -- pure
R' Yochanan: as the dispute regarding impurity, so the dispute regarding Shabbat
R' Yochanan: but not regarding chalitza

supports.gloss_en: כדרב יהודה -- as Abaye ruled for Rav Yehuda's sandals, worn by him and by his child: permitted ab initio
מדקמתרץ רבי יוחנן אליבא דרבי יהודה -- since R' Yochanan extends R' Yehuda's view to Shabbat, the halakha follows R' Yehuda

objections.gloss_en: קשיא מנעל אמנעל -- the baraitot on a shoe contradict: liable, exempt but forbidden (p_b_patur), permitted ab initio

answered_by.gloss_en: מנעל אמנעל לא קשיא: liable -- a shoemakers' [knot]; exempt but forbidden -- the Rabbis'; permitted -- the people of Mechoza's (= p_ok_mindal_chayav, p_ok_mindal_patur, p_ok_mindal_mutar)

objections.gloss_en: קשיא סנדל אסנדל -- the baraitot on a sandal contradict: liable, exempt but forbidden (p_b_patur), permitted ab initio

answered_by.gloss_en: סנדל אסנדל לא קשיא: liable -- Arabs' [sandals] that shoemakers tie; exempt but forbidden -- what they tie themselves; permitted -- a sandal two people go out in (= p_ok_sandal_chayav, p_ok_sandal_patur, p_ok_sandal_mutar)

objections.gloss_en: השתא פטור אבל אסור קא קשיא לי, חייב חטאת קאמרת לי?! -- on weekdays too he and his child both wear the sandal, so its knot is not permanent; Abaye: אי הכי, מותר לכתחילה
מאי שנא מדרבי ירמיה? -- R' Abbahu let R' Yirmeya wrap a reed on his torn sandal; why must Abaye leave his?

answered_by.gloss_en: התם לא מינטר, הכא מינטר -- there the sandal would not be guarded, here it is (= p_minatar)

objections.gloss_en: והא מנא הוא, דאי בעינא הפיכנא ליה מימין לשמאל? -- the torn sandal is still a vessel, since it can be worn on the other foot

answered_by.gloss_en: מדקמתרץ רבי יוחנן אליבא דרבי יהודה, שמע מינה הלכה כרבי יהודה -- and per R' Yehuda an outer strap broken renders the sandal pure, i.e. no longer a vessel (= p_halakha_kerabbi_yehuda)
